image_description: A close-up, black-and-white photograph of a metallic flip-top lighter (resembling a Zippo style) with its lid open. A bright, stylized flame emerges from the top right. The body features a perforated wind guard design and embossed text reading 'GREKKE' on the front face. The background is a smooth, out-of-focus gradient.

artifact_observations.location: Front face of the lighter body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The embossed text reads 'GREKKE', which is likely a hallucinated brand name. The letterforms are slightly irregular and lack the sharp, crisp edges of real industrial stamping, showing slight melting into the metal texture.

The flame does not anchor correctly to a physical wick or nozzle. It appears to emanate from the side of the rim rather than the center, and the base of the flame blends softly into the metal without a clear combustion point.
The circular holes on the upper casing vary slightly in shape and depth consistency, appearing somewhat painted on rather than physically punched through the metal thickness.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the flame's interaction with the lighter. Real flames anchor to a wick; AI flames often float or merge with the casing. Check if the perforated holes show any thickness or if they look like flat circles.
